Our research bot read three point five hours as thirty-five.
By the time anyone noticed, it was in a Short, two posts, the landing page, its preview image, and a waitlist email. Tens of thousands of people had seen it.
So we treat a wrong claim like a product recall.
Every source, every claim quoted from it, and everything we shipped on top of it.
A QA agent checks receipts. The number has to be in the quote. Thirty-five isn't. Ten thousand teams has no source at all.
One correction. FalkorDB walks every derived-from path, at any depth.
Then the recall plan. Every live item, who owns it, and about how many people saw it. Most-viewed first: fix the Short before the reply thread.
The FAQ stays clean. No path, no recall.
At twenty-six thousand nodes and ten hops, the cascade takes about six tenths of a millisecond, and the full recall plan about fifteen.
Why is the Short wrong? Short, script, blog, brief, claim, and the exact source line.
Each fix goes back to whoever made it.
A few lines of Cypher, exposed over MCP to any agent.
Taint plus Receipts. One wrong number, every place it reached, biggest audience first.
